source.title: Optimization Variance: Exploring Generalization Properties of DNNs
source.authors: Xiao Zhang; Dong-Rui Wu; Haoyi Xiong; Bo Dai

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test performance over training epochs and network widths, but uses its own noisy-label setups and zero-one loss/bias-variance analysis rather than reproducing the original study's full method.
record.gate_note: Rows record the study's own test-performance results. References to other studies' findings are not included. OV and bias/variance values are not treated as test-error results; the paper's reported OV–accuracy correlation is included only where it directly reports the network-width comparison.
record.test_reason: The study measures expected test zero-one error over training epochs for six ResNet/VGG settings with and without label noise, with its own bias-variance method. Its results bear directly on epoch-wise double descent (V2) and its dependence on label noise and variance (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that variance, not bias, dominates epoch-wise double descent of the test zero-one error and correlates highly with it. They propose optimization variance, computed from the training set only, to predict test error during training and to early-stop without a validation set.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes epoch-wise behavior using zero-one-loss bias-variance decomposition and introduces optimization variance; its width experiment is a separate ResNet18 sweep. It does not reproduce the original study's full experimental recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The presence and prominence of epoch-wise double descent vary with label-noise level; the paper also reports different behaviors across optimizer and learning-rate settings in appendices.

fits_no_version.finding: In the small CNN on CIFAR10 subsets, more training samples (2000 to 6000) give better test accuracy. No interpolation threshold is located.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the reported small-CNN CIFAR10 setup, increasing the training-set size across the tested counts improves generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the zero-one bias-variance decomposition, the variance term alone tracks the epoch-wise test-error curve, while bias falls and plateaus.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The epoch-wise double-descent shape of test zero-one error is mirrored by the variance term, not the bias term.

record.problems: Many relevant curve values are presented only in figures. The bias-variance experiments use training sets sampled at 50% of the available training data, and the authors caution that behavior may differ when the full training set is used. The width result is limited to one architecture and dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results were omitted. Appendix plots about bias/variance and optimization variance were not added as test-error rows because they measure those quantities rather than the test-error behavior named by the claim.

untested.parts: The width sweep (r1) does not span or locate the interpolation threshold and uses no label noise, so the model-wise peak is not tested.
Sample counts 2000/4000/6000 use one small CNN with no interpolation threshold established. Only 'more data helps' is reported (r22-r24).
No single effective-complexity measure is tested against peak locations. OV is a training-set proxy and is not tested as a predictor of peak position across axes.
Multiple or triple descent, and removal of the peak by optimally tuned regularization, are not tested.
No re-expression of complexity via an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Test ZO loss vs CE and MSE loss over epochs. Double descent is clear on ZO but barely observable on CE/MSE.
Test loss over epochs across several label-noise levels. Noise level reportedly does not shift the epoch of the first loss minimum.
Expected test ZO loss over epochs with Adam lr 1e-3 and SGD lr 1e-2/1e-3 at 20% noise. VGG11 on SVHN with Adam 1e-3 failed to train.
missing.locator: Appendix H, Figures 13-15; Appendix D, Figure 9

record.verdict_notes: Bias-variance estimates use five models trained on 50% subsamples of the training set. Authors caution that behaviour may differ with the full training set. Rows r14-r19 duplicate the Fig. 1 noisy settings in accuracy form. r20-r21 (LeNet, no noise) show only spikes, not a fall-rise-fall shape. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests a width sweep for one ResNet18 setting, but does not locate an interpolation threshold or report whether the pattern generalizes across models and datasets.
Tests are on the reported datasets, architectures, label-noise levels, and training procedures only.
The small-training-set experiment does not establish whether its sample counts are near an interpolation threshold.
Only deep neural networks are studied; other model classes are not tested.
The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study varies label-noise levels, but does not test multiple/triple descent or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The study does not re-express complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that makes the curve an ordinary U.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.size_stated: For each convolutional layer, filters set to k/4 times the original number, k = 1, 2, ..., 8
rows.operation_detail: Compared network widths on CIFAR10.
rows.note: The authors state that as k increases, OV decreases and increasing network size improves generalization; the figure plots test accuracy against width. The reported sweep does not describe a fall-rise-fall test-error pattern.
rows.check: The width sweep runs k/4 to 2x the original ResNet18 width, with no label noise. The paper never locates an interpolation threshold, and these widths likely all lie past it. Monotone improvement here cannot show whether a peak exists, so 'reversed' is unsupported.
